outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no proof, disproof or counterexample to the section conjecture as stated has appeared in the sources I could read; the in-window events are a Chabauty–Kim proof of an S-Selmer variant for one open curve over imaginary quadratic fields (Li and Lüdtke, arXiv 20 Aug 2026), a p-adic toric analogue (Bresciani, v1 12 Sep 2024, current v5 14 Sep 2026), and neighbouring or variant work, while Bresciani's index-1 twisted-form result, first posted May 2023, was published in the Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux in April 2026.
problem_asks: As worded in the frozen statement: the splittings (sections) of the group homomorphism from the fundamental group of a complete smooth curve X over a finitely generated field k to the Galois group of k. Unpacked: (a) surjectivity: every such splitting, up to conjugacy, comes from a k-rational point of X, i.e. the Kummer map X(k) to splittings modulo conjugacy is onto, for every complete smooth curve over every finitely generated field k; (b) injectivity: distinct k-points give non-conjugate splittings. The statement says only 'describes splittings', but the conjecture is usually stated as a bijection, so both halves are listed. Injectivity is recorded as known for hyperbolic curves over such fields (Grothendieck, via Mordell–Weil, per the search snippets); surjectivity is the open part. (c) Quantifiers: all complete smooth curves and all finitely generated fields. The statement names no genus; the Wikipedia lead restricts to genus at least 2, and I read that lead as a 2026 revision, not the frozen wording. The statement does not say characteristic zero; the sources read all work in characteristic zero.

events.what_happened: Xiang Li and Martin Lüdtke, ‘Polylogarithmic Chabauty–Kim loci over number fields’, arXiv:2608.20615 (v1, 20 Aug 2026, math.NT, 69 pp). Among other things it gives a Chabauty–Kim proof of the S-Selmer Section Conjecture for X = P¹ minus {0,1,∞} over imaginary quadratic fields K, when S is empty or a single prime not fixed by complex conjugation (stated as Theorem 1.4(c), proved in Theorem 8.28, per the HTML text). It also verifies Kim’s conjecture in some new cases and shows the method is insufficient in others.
events.delivers: Establishes the S-Selmer Section Conjecture (a variant using Selmer sections and S-integral data) for one curve, the thrice-punctured line, over imaginary quadratic fields, for S empty or a single prime not stable under complex conjugation. Restrictions: the curve is open (P¹ minus three points), not the complete smooth curve of the statement; only Selmer sections are covered; only imaginary quadratic base fields; only those S.
events.remains: Every other complete smooth curve; every finitely generated field other than these imaginary quadratic fields; sections that are not Selmer; larger S; surjectivity for complete curves in general.
events.doubts: No public engagement found. The result depends on explicit depth-2 polylogarithmic equations, some of which the paper says GPT-5.5 helped discover (Theorem 9.8). I could not read Sections 6–12 of the HTML, so I could not check whether Theorem 8.28 depends on Theorem 9.8. The fetched text reportedly says these instances are not new (Remark 8.29); not checked against the full text.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture (the S-Selmer variant holds) for one open curve over imaginary quadratic fields. No counterexample.

systems.name: GPT-5.5
systems.what_it_did: The paper says GPT-5.5 was used to discover the equations and coefficient formulas in Theorem 9.8. The same disclosure says GPT and other large language models helped write some SageMath code, and that all AI-assisted output was checked and verified by the authors. Whether Theorem 9.8 is needed for the S-Selmer result (Theorem 8.28) was not established.
systems.basis_quote: GPT-5.5 was also used to discover the equations and coefficient formulas in Theorem 9.8.

events.what_happened: Giulio Bresciani, ‘The section conjecture for the toric fundamental group over p-adic fields’, arXiv:2409.07923. The paper proves a toric analogue over finite extensions of Q_p. Per the v5 HTML, Theorem 1.3 gives bijectivity of the toric Kummer map for abelian torsors, and Theorem 1.4 states the same for smooth projective hyperbolic curves. Its abstract says a resolution of the toric section conjecture would reduce the original to particular cases. The author presented it at RIMS Kyoto on 1 June 2026.
events.revisions: v2 19 Sep 2024; v3 10 Oct 2024, listed as withdrawn (1 KB); v4 1 May 2025; v5 14 Sep 2026 (current). The arXiv comment says: The first versions of the paper contained a serious mistake, spotted by Y. Hoshi and A. Tamagawa.
events.delivers: For the toric fundamental group over finite extensions of Q_p: the toric Kummer map is bijective for abelian torsors (Theorem 1.3, v5). For hyperbolic curves the v5 HTML reads as Theorem 1.4 giving bijectivity, but the June 2026 talk abstract says only that the toric conjecture is supported by strong evidence for hyperbolic curves. This conflict is not resolved. Scope: p-adic base fields, which are not finitely generated over Q, and the toric group, not the étale fundamental group.
events.remains: The étale section conjecture for any curve over any field; the statement's finitely generated fields; the toric statement for hyperbolic curves if Theorem 1.4 is not as read.

checked_by.who: Yuichiro Hoshi (RIMS, Kyoto) and Akio Tamagawa
checked_by.qualification: Leading anabelian geometers working on this conjecture
checked_by.what_they_did: Found a serious mistake in earlier versions, as the paper’s acknowledgements and arXiv comment say. The paper does not say they verified the current version.

events.time_since_posted: about 13 months since v1; v5 posted 14 Sep 2026
events.doubts: Earlier versions contained a serious mistake, so v1 and v2 should not be relied on; v3 is listed as withdrawn with no reason given. The conflict over whether hyperbolic curves are covered is noted under delivers. The v5 HTML does not describe the earlier mistake, and I could not read the proof of Theorem 1.4.

withdrawn.what: arXiv v3 (10 Oct 2024) listed as withdrawn, no reason given

events.direction: An analogue for a different group over different base fields. It cuts in favour of the toric analogue for abelian varieties and, on the v5 reading, for hyperbolic curves over p-adic fields. No counterexample. It bears on the étale statement only through a claimed reduction.

systems.name: ChatGPT 5.6
systems.what_it_did: The AI disclosure (Section 1.6) says the results of Section 9 (towers in abelian varieties, including Theorem 9.1) were obtained in collaboration with the model; that the first draft of Section 12 (Tannakian interpretation of the toric fundamental group) was written by it under the author’s guidance and then edited by the author; and that it reviewed the paper and spotted several minor mistakes. The fetched text says the proof of Theorem 1.3 (Section 8) does not use Section 9. Whether Section 9 feeds Theorem 1.4 could not be read.
systems.basis_quote: The results of section 9 were obtained in collaboration with ChatGPT 5.6 (see Remark 9.5 for details).

events.what_happened: Giulio Bresciani, ‘On Grothendieck’s section conjecture for curves of index 1’, arXiv:2305.10088 (v1, 17 May 2023; the only arXiv version). Published in Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 38 (2026), 295–316 (received 19 Dec 2024, revised 19 Oct 2025, accepted 7 Nov 2025, published 24 Apr 2026). Main results: every hyperbolic curve with a faithful action of a non-cyclic p-group has a twisted form of index 1 satisfying the conjecture; for every hyperbolic curve S over a finitely generated field k over Q there is a finite extension K/k and a finite étale cover C → S_K satisfying the conjecture.
events.revisions: Only arXiv v1 is listed. The journal abstract says ‘Given an odd prime p’; the arXiv v1 had exceptions for p=2 with extra conditions. The journal version is dated 24 Apr 2026.
events.delivers: Establishes the conjecture for some twisted forms of index 1 of hyperbolic curves that carry a non-cyclic p-group action. A twisted form is a different curve over the same field, so this is not the curve itself. For any hyperbolic curve over a finitely generated field over Q, it gives the conjecture for a finite étale cover over a finite extension, not for the curve itself. Per the journal abstract, earlier proved cases all had no rational points and index different from 1, so these are index-1 cases.
events.remains: The conjecture for the curves themselves (not twisted forms or covers); all hyperbolic curves over all finitely generated fields; the p=2 cases in the journal version; complete curves of genus 0 or 1, which are not addressed in what I read.

checked_by.who: Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux (editorial refereeing; referees not named on the page)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper on 7 Nov 2025 and published it on 24 Apr 2026

checked_by.qualification: Leading expert on the section conjecture; author of the monograph Rational Points and Arithmetic of Fundamental Groups
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave comments that the author says substantially improved the exposition (acknowledgements). No verification is claimed.

events.time_since_posted: about 3 years 5 months since arXiv v1; about 6 months since journal publication
events.doubts: No active doubt found. The results are about twisted forms and covers, not the curves themselves, which a reader could treat as a restricted case.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for specified families (twisted forms of index 1 and covers). No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Giulio Bresciani, ‘On the birational section conjecture with strong birationality assumptions’, arXiv:2108.13397 (v1 30 Aug 2021; v2 12 Feb 2022; v3 15 Sep 2023). Published in Inventiones mathematicae (2023), DOI 10.1007/s00222-023-01220-6. For a curve over a finitely generated field k over Q, a section whose base change to k(t) is birationally liftable comes from geometry. The abstract says the section conjecture is equivalent to cuspidalization of all sections over all finitely generated fields.
events.revisions: v2 12 Feb 2022; v3 15 Sep 2023 (final version); journal Inventiones mathematicae 2023
events.delivers: A birational-version result under an extra hypothesis (birational liftability after base change to k(t)). It does not prove the non-birational section conjecture. Its corollary is an equivalence with the cuspidalization conjecture, which is a reduction.
events.remains: The section conjecture itself, since the equivalence leaves cuspidalization open; the birational version without the strong hypothesis.
events.direction: A reduction for the birational variant, with a conditional equivalence to cuspidalization. It does not decide the question. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Giulio Bresciani, ‘On the section conjecture over fields of finite type’, arXiv:1911.03234 (v1 8 Nov 2019; v2 25 Jun 2021; v3 1 Mar 2023). Assuming the section conjecture over number fields, it proves the conjecture for a broad class of curves over finitely generated extensions of Q: all projective hyperelliptic curves, hyperbolic affine curves of genus at most 2, and a nonempty open subset of any curve. With the weak Bombieri–Lang conjecture added, it covers every hyperbolic curve over every finitely generated extension of Q. An SNS repository record lists a 2025 published version; the journal is not identified, because the page returned HTTP 403.
events.revisions: v2 25 Jun 2021; v3 1 Mar 2023; SNS repository lists a 2025 published version (journal unidentified)
events.delivers: A conditional reduction. Given the number-field case, the conjecture holds for the named class of curves over finitely generated fields over Q. Adding weak Bombieri–Lang gives all hyperbolic curves over such fields, still conditionally.
events.remains: The number-field case, which is assumed and open; the rest of the curves over finitely generated fields without Bombieri–Lang; complete curves of genus 0 or 1.

checked_by.qualification: Journal not named; record not readable
checked_by.what_they_did: Published, per the SNS repository record as seen in search results

events.doubts: Journal and refereeing unverified. The result is conditional on the number-field case and on Bombieri–Lang for the full version.
events.direction: Conditional support for the conjecture for a class of curves. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Giulio Bresciani, ‘On the section conjecture and Brauer–Severi varieties’, arXiv:2106.07397 (14 June 2021; one version), Mathematische Zeitschrift (2021), DOI 10.1007/s00209-021-02835-2. For a positive-genus curve X over a number field k: if the Weil restriction R_{k/Q}X admits a rational map to a non-trivial Brauer–Severi variety, then X satisfies the section conjecture. This extends Stix’s result over Q.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv; Mathematische Zeitschrift 2021
events.delivers: The conjecture for a class of curves over number fields (those whose Weil restriction maps to a non-trivial Brauer–Severi variety), plus a corollary for curves mapping to a Brauer–Severi variety with non-trivial corestriction.
events.remains: All other curves over number fields and all curves over other finitely generated fields.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for a class of curves over number fields. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: L. Alexander Betts and Jakob Stix, ‘Galois sections and p-adic period mappings’, arXiv:2204.13674 (v1 28 Apr 2022; the only arXiv version). Annals of Mathematics 201 (2025), no. 1, 79–166 (received 20 Jul 2022, revised 24 May 2024, accepted 28 May 2024, published online 9 Jan 2025). For a number field K not containing a CM subfield and a smooth projective curve Y/K of genus at least 2, the image of the Selmer part of the section set in Y(K_v) is finite at every finite place v. This is an unconditional verification of a prediction of the section conjecture. The method refines Lawrence–Venkatesh.
events.revisions: Only arXiv v1 is listed. The Annals version was revised on 24 May 2024 and accepted on 28 May 2024.
events.delivers: A finiteness statement: the images of Selmer sections are finite at each finite place, for genus at least 2 curves over number fields without a CM subfield. It does not show that Selmer sections are geometric, and does not give the bijection. It covers only Selmer sections and number fields.
events.remains: Whether every Selmer section is geometric (surjectivity); all non-Selmer sections; number fields with a CM subfield; finitely generated fields that are not number fields.

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted on 28 May 2024 and published in 2025

events.doubts: No active doubt found. The result is a partial finiteness statement, not a resolution of the bijection.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture (finiteness of Selmer-section images). Not a bijection. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: L. Alexander Betts, Theresa Kumpitsch and Martin Lüdtke, ‘Chabauty–Kim, finite descent, and the Section Conjecture for locally geometric sections’, arXiv:2305.09462 (v1 16 May 2023, titled Chabauty–Kim and the Section Conjecture for locally geometric sections; v2 11 Apr 2026, comment: minor revision, appendix rewritten, finite descent added to the title). For a smooth projective genus at least 2 curve over a number field, the locally geometric variant holds if Kim’s conjecture holds for almost all auxiliary primes p. It extends to S-integral points on hyperbolic curves and is carried out for the thrice-punctured line over Z[1/2]. Lüdtke also gave a talk at SNS Pisa in Oct 2024 on this work; a talk is not a written argument.
events.revisions: v2 11 Apr 2026 (minor revision; appendix rewritten; finite descent added to title)
events.delivers: Conditional: the locally geometric variant of the section conjecture for X over Q, and its S-integral generalisation, follow from Kim’s conjecture for almost all auxiliary primes p. The thrice-punctured-line example over Z[1/2] is treated per the abstract. Restrictions: sections that are locally geometric everywhere (a variant), and the result is conditional on Kim’s conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture for all sections, meaning sections that are not locally geometric (the abstract’s second problem; a search snippet says it amounts to the p-adic section conjecture, not verified); Kim’s conjecture itself; the complete-curve statement in general.
events.time_since_posted: about 3 years 5 months since v1; v2 about 6 months ago
events.doubts: Conditional on Kim’s conjecture for almost all primes, which is itself open. No review or verification found. One 2026 paper cites v2 (identity not established from the snippet).
events.direction: Conditional support for the locally geometric variant. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Simon Shuofeng Xu, ‘Section conjectures over C and Kodaira fibrations’, arXiv:2407.03248 (v1 3 Jul 2024; v2 23 Jul 2024; v3 20 Oct 2025, a major revision with an appendix by Seraphina Eun Bi Lee and Carlos A. Serván). It proposes topological and Hodge-theoretic analogues over C. For families of curves, injectivity holds for both analogues. Topological surjectivity fails: Corollary 4.0.10 gives counterexamples with no algebraic sections. For families of Jacobians the topological surjectivity fails in general.
events.revisions: v2 23 Jul 2024; v3 20 Oct 2025 (major revision, new appendix)
events.delivers: Analogues over C, which is not finitely generated over Q. For curve families, injectivity of both analogues; topological surjectivity fails for some families (Kodaira fibrations).
events.remains: The arithmetic conjecture over finitely generated fields, which the complex analogue does not address.
events.doubts: The appendix authors are co-authors, not independent referees. No review found.
events.direction: The complex analogue fails on surjectivity for some families. That is a counterexample to an analogue over C, not to the statement's arithmetic conjecture. Whether it bears on the statement is for the judging pass.
events.object: Families of curves over C (Kodaira fibrations) for which the topological section map is not surjective; Corollary 4.0.10 says counterexamples to the surjectivity part of the topological section question with no algebraic sections exist (appendix by Lee and Serván). The construction is in a section titled ‘Some construction of Kodaira fibrations’; I did not read it. Not described as explicit in the text read.

events.what_happened: Jesse Pajwani, ‘The Valuative Section Conjecture, Étale Homotopy, and Berkovich Spaces’, arXiv:2304.03970 (v1 8 Apr 2023; v2 16 Aug 2023; v3 2 Jul 2024). Published in Homology, Homotopy and Applications 27 (2025), 261–288. It reinterprets a result of Pop and Stix on the p-adic section conjecture using Berkovich spaces and fixed points, extends it to larger classes of fields, and gives a valuative section-conjecture-type result for a larger class of varieties.
events.revisions: v2 16 Aug 2023; v3 2 Jul 2024 (25 pp); journal HHA 2025
events.delivers: A valuative (p-adic-type) version for fields that are not finitely generated over Q, per the abstract. The abstract does not address the statement’s finitely generated fields.
events.remains: The statement for finitely generated fields; the bijection in general.
events.direction: A valuative version over non-finitely-generated fields. Consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample; not the statement’s class.

events.what_happened: Martin Lüdtke, ‘Refined Chabauty–Kim computations for the thrice-punctured line over Z[1/6]’, arXiv:2402.03573 (v1 5 Feb 2024; v2 13 Jul 2024). Published in Research in Number Theory 11 (2025), 24. It verifies Kim’s conjecture over Z[1/6] for all auxiliary primes p < 10,000.
events.revisions: v2 13 Jul 2024; journal Research in Number Theory 2025
events.delivers: Verifies Kim’s conjecture, not the section conjecture, for one open curve over Z[1/6] for finitely many auxiliary primes (p < 10,000). Finitely many instances of a claim about all primes do not settle that claim.
events.remains: Kim’s conjecture for all auxiliary primes; the section conjecture.
events.direction: A different question (Kim’s conjecture), with finitely many instances checked. Not a section result.

events.what_happened: Wojciech Porowski, ‘On reductions of Selmer sections’, arXiv:2509.15660 (v1, 19 Sep 2025; no journal reference). For a hyperbolic curve over a number field: a noncuspidal Selmer section is determined up to conjugacy by its reduction on a set of density one (Theorem 1.1), and reduces to cusps only on a set of density zero after a finite extension (Theorem 1.2). The HTML introduction calls the Grothendieck section conjecture a major open problem in anabelian geometry.
events.delivers: Results on Selmer sections, a variant of the sections the statement asks about: conjugacy determined by reduction on density-one sets, and reduction to cusps on density-zero sets.
events.remains: Surjectivity of the Kummer map; non-Selmer sections; the statement in full.
events.direction: Partial results on Selmer sections, consistent with the conjecture; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Ryoji Shimizu and Naganori Yamaguchi, ‘Étale fundamental groups of smooth arithmetic surfaces and the Grothendieck conjecture’, arXiv:2511.06725 (v1 10 Nov 2025; v2 7 Jun 2026). A relative version of the Grothendieck anabelian conjecture for smooth curves over certain arithmetic schemes; hyperbolic curves over S-integers of number fields with a rational prime inverted are anabelian; a partial result toward the semi-absolute version. A DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2026.07.007 is listed; the journal was not checked.
events.delivers: An anabelian (isomorphism-type) statement about curves and their fundamental groups, not about sections. A neighbouring problem.
events.remains: The section conjecture, entirely.
events.direction: A different question (the Grothendieck isomorphism conjecture). Not about sections.

events.what_happened: Naganori Yamaguchi, ‘The metabelian Grothendieck conjecture for genus zero curves over finitely generated fields’, arXiv:2407.09906 (v1 13 Jul 2024; v2 14 Jul 2026). It proves the metabelian isomorphism version of the Grothendieck conjecture for genus-zero hyperbolic curves over finitely generated fields.
events.delivers: A metabelian isomorphism statement for genus-zero curves. Not about sections.
events.remains: The section conjecture.
events.direction: A different question (the isomorphism conjecture). Not a section result.

I found the titles and schedule only. The abstracts were not retrieved, and no written paper was found.
events.delivers: Not established. The content of the talks is unknown to this record.
events.remains: Unknown.
events.doubts: The titles say ‘Progress on Section Conjecture’, so they may report results. Not checked.
events.direction: Unknown. The talk titles do not indicate direction.

events.what_happened: Florian Pop, note on the t-birational section conjecture, file dated 28 Sep 2025 on Pop’s Penn page. The PDF returned HTTP 403, so I know it only from a search snippet. The snippet says it gives generalisations and minimalistic refinements of the t-birational section conjecture over general base fields, including finitely generated fields over Q.
events.delivers: Not verified: the PDF was not readable. A birational variant, a neighbouring question.
events.remains: Not verified.
events.doubts: Read only through a search snippet.
events.direction: Birational variant; not the non-birational statement.

events.what_happened: Jakob Stix, ‘The Brauer–Manin obstruction for sections of the fundamental group’, arXiv:0910.5009 (26 Oct 2009; one version; no journal reference). It establishes Grothendieck’s section conjecture for an open subset of the Reichardt–Lind curve and introduces a Brauer–Manin obstruction for sections of the fundamental group extension.
events.delivers: The conjecture for an open subset of one specific curve (the Reichardt–Lind curve). The abstract page does not state the base field, so whether it is finitely generated is not verified.
events.remains: The complete curve; all other curves; the general conjecture.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for an open subset of one specific curve. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Jochen Koenigsmann, ‘On the section conjecture in anabelian geometry’, arXiv:math/0305226 (15 May 2003; one version, 21 pp; no journal reference). It proves the birational section conjecture in some settings (the abstract gives the p-adic numbers as an example), and disproves both the section and the birational conjecture for the fields of all real or p-adic algebraic numbers.
events.delivers: The birational version over local fields such as the p-adic numbers, which are outside the statement’s class. The disproof covers the fields of all real or p-adic algebraic numbers, which are not finitely generated over Q. The statement’s finitely generated fields are not addressed.
events.remains: The section conjecture for finitely generated fields over Q.
events.direction: A disproof for field classes that are not finitely generated over Q. The judging pass decides whether it bears on the statement.

events.what_happened: Yuichiro Hoshi, ‘Existence of Nongeometric Pro-p Galois Sections of Hyperbolic Curves’, Publications of the RIMS, Kyoto University 46 (2010), 829–848 (submitted 18 Jan 2010; published 18 Nov 2010). It constructs a nongeometric pro-p Galois section of a proper hyperbolic curve over a number field (and over a p-adic local field), and gives a negative answer to the pro-p version of the section conjecture.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the pro-p variant on a number-field curve. This is about pro-p Galois sections, not all Galois sections, so it does not settle the full statement.
events.remains: The full section conjecture for finitely generated fields.
events.direction: A counterexample to the pro-p variant. It cuts against that variant, not against the full statement.
events.object: A nongeometric pro-p Galois section of a proper hyperbolic curve over a number field, from the construction in the paper. The abstract gives infinitely many conjugacy classes of such sections for some curve. The construction is not described on the abstract page.

events.what_happened: Mohamed Saïdi, ‘On the section conjecture over function fields and finitely generated fields’, arXiv:1512.01207 (v1 3 Dec 2015; v2 22 Mar 2016; v3 14 Feb 2017), Publications of the RIMS, Kyoto University 52 (2016), 335–357. The section conjecture over finitely generated fields over Q follows from the number-field case, given finiteness of the ℓ-primary parts of certain Shafarevich–Tate groups. Unconditionally, if it holds for all number fields then it holds over all finitely generated fields for curves defined over a number field.
events.delivers: A reduction. Conditional for the general finitely generated case (Shafarevich–Tate finiteness). Partial unconditional reduction for curves defined over number fields.
events.remains: The number-field case itself, which is open; the conditional part for curves not defined over number fields.
events.direction: A reduction, consistent with the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Mohamed Saïdi and Michael Tyler, ‘On the birational section conjecture over finitely generated fields’, arXiv:1909.12099 (Sep 2019). Per search snippets, the birational section conjecture over finitely generated fields over Q follows from the number-field case, with a criterion involving finite Shafarevich–Tate groups for the Jacobian. Not opened.
events.delivers: A birational reduction, read from a search snippet only. Not the non-birational statement.
events.remains: The non-birational conjecture.
events.doubts: Not opened; the snippet is the only evidence.
events.direction: A birational reduction. Not the non-birational statement.

events.what_happened: Jakob Stix, ‘On the birational section conjecture with local conditions’, arXiv:1203.3236 (March 2012, per the arXiv identifier). Per a search snippet, the birational section conjecture holds for birationally adelic noncuspidal Galois sections when the base field is totally real or imaginary quadratic; published in Inventiones (2015) per snippet. Not opened.
events.delivers: Birational result over totally real or imaginary quadratic fields, read from a snippet. Not the non-birational statement.
events.remains: The non-birational conjecture; other base fields.
events.direction: Birational support over specified fields. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Hélène Esnault and Olivier Wittenberg, ‘On abelian birational sections’, Journal of the American Mathematical Society 23 (2010). Per search snippets, over number fields with finite Tate–Shafarevich group of the Picard variety, abelian birational sections exist iff the elementary Brauer–Manin obstruction vanishes. Earliest arXiv posting not checked; not opened.
events.delivers: A birational, abelianised statement, read from snippets. Not the non-birational statement.
events.remains: The non-birational conjecture.
events.doubts: Not opened; year is the journal year.
events.direction: Birational, abelian; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Stefan Patrikis, José Felipe Voloch and Yuri Zarhin, ‘Anabelian geometry and descent obstructions on moduli spaces’, arXiv:1506.04379 (v1 14 Jun 2015; v4 26 May 2016), Algebra & Number Theory 10 (2016), 1191–1219. Assuming several well-known conjectures (Hodge, Tate, Fontaine–Mazur, Grothendieck–Serre), the section conjecture fails for moduli spaces of principally polarised abelian varieties, and the finite descent obstruction explains the Hasse failure for a class of adelic points. For curves, the finite descent sufficiency is shown to imply the same for all hyperbolic curves.
events.revisions: v4 26 May 2016; journal Algebra & Number Theory 2016
events.delivers: A conditional failure for moduli spaces of principally polarised abelian varieties, which are not curves. Not a statement about curves over finitely generated fields.
events.remains: Curves over finitely generated fields.
events.doubts: The failure is conditional on several well-known conjectures.
events.direction: A conditional failure for a different variety (moduli spaces). It does not bear on curves over finitely generated fields.

events.what_happened: Feng-Wen An, ‘On the section conjecture of Grothendieck’, arXiv:0911.1523 (v1 9 Nov 2009; v4 20 Dec 2009; 22 pp; no journal reference). Using monodromy actions on a universal cover of the étale fundamental group and on an sp-completion, it claims ‘a proof of the section conjecture of Grothendieck for arithmetic schemes’.
events.delivers: As claimed: the section conjecture for arithmetic schemes, which are of finite type and surjective over Spec Z. That class would include curves over number fields if the claim is correct. Not verified; no acceptance found.
events.remains: Unknown; depends on whether the claim is correct.
events.doubts: No journal, review, or published verification found. The claim covers a much broader class than curves, and the monodromy construction was not checked. Later sources in the window treat the conjecture as open; the Porowski April 2026 notes are seen only through a snippet.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture for a broader class. Not accepted in any source found.

events.what_happened: Florian Pop and Jakob Stix, valuative version of the p-adic section conjecture for curves over p-adic local fields (preprint, 2011). The image of every section lies in the decomposition subgroup of some valuation prolonging the p-adic valuation to the function field. disputes.summary: Feng-Wen An (2009, arXiv:0911.1523) claims a proof of Grothendieck’s section conjecture for arithmetic schemes. No journal, review, or verification was found, and the other sources read in the window treat the conjecture as open. Not resolved here.

Bresciani’s toric paper (arXiv:2409.07923) says an earlier version contained a serious mathematical mistake, spotted by Y. Hoshi and A. Tamagawa. The current version keeps results it says are unaffected. The mistake is not described on the pages I read.

Whether the toric analogue is proved for hyperbolic curves over p-adic fields. The v5 HTML gives Theorem 1.4 as a bijectivity statement; the June 2026 talk abstract says only that strong evidence exists for hyperbolic curves.

summary: I ran 46 web searches and opened arXiv abstracts and, where the tool could render them, HTML full texts for the key papers; the PDF tools returned binary for most arXiv PDFs, so full texts were read only in part. No source reports a proof, disproof or counterexample to the section conjecture for complete smooth curves over finitely generated fields, and injectivity is recorded as known. The record is mostly partial and variant results. The most important in-window item is Li and Lüdtke (arXiv:2608.20615, 20 Aug 2026), which gives a Chabauty–Kim proof of the S-Selmer section conjecture for P¹ minus three points over imaginary quadratic fields. That is a Selmer variant on an open curve, not the statement. I count it as a restricted case, and the judging pass decides. Bresciani’s index-1 result (first posted May 2023, published April 2026) is a second close call: it gives the conjecture for twisted forms and covers of index-1 curves, not for the curves themselves, and both readings are recorded. Bresciani’s toric paper (v1 Sep 2024, current v5 14 Sep 2026) is an analogue over p-adic fields, which are not finitely generated over Q. Its earlier versions had a serious mistake, and its hyperbolic-curve claim is described inconsistently across sources. Other partial results are older and recorded as events: Betts–Stix finiteness for Selmer sections (Annals 2025), Saïdi’s reductions (2015), Bresciani’s conditional class results (2019, 2021), and the Betts–Kumpitsch–Lüdtke conditional locally geometric variant (2023; v2 Apr 2026). Feng-Wen An’s 2009 claim for arithmetic schemes is unaccepted. Neighbouring but different questions are recorded as events and excluded from the section record: Kim’s conjecture (Lüdtke 2024), anabelian isomorphism results (Shimizu–Yamaguchi 2025, Yamaguchi 2024), Porowski’s Selmer reduction preprint (Sep 2025), and Xu’s complex analogue (2024; surjectivity fails for some families). AI involvement: no source connects an AI system with the section conjecture itself. The AI-lab announcements and AI-math trackers I searched (OpenAI’s Astra and Erdős unit-distance results, DeepMind’s AlphaProof Nexus, Epoch’s FrontierMath Erdős set) do not mention it, and no Lean formalisation of it was found. Two in-window papers do disclose AI. Li and Lüdtke say GPT-5.5 was used to discover the equations and coefficient formulas in Theorem 9.8, and that GPT and other large language models helped write some SageMath code; all AI output was checked by the authors. I could not read whether Theorem 8.28 (the S-Selmer result) depends on Theorem 9.8. Bresciani’s toric paper says ChatGPT 5.6 collaborated on the Section 9 results, wrote a first draft of Section 12 and reviewed the paper; the fetched text says the proof of its Theorem 1.3 does not use Section 9, and its role in Theorem 1.4 could not be read. Both are recorded in ai.systems for their events, and the judging pass decides whether either is load-bearing. Porowski’s April 2026 RIMS lecture notes describe the conjecture as open; the PDF was binary to the tools, so I used only search snippets for that. Hoshi gave two 2025 talks titled Progress on Section Conjecture I and II; I could not retrieve the abstracts, and they are the most important unread item.
competing_reading: A generous reader would count Li and Lüdtke (2026) and Bresciani’s index-1 result (in print 2026) as in-window progress on the conjecture: each proves it for specified curves or classes, and the first is a Chabauty–Kim proof for an actual curve. A strict reader would say neither settles any complete smooth curve over a finitely generated field, since the first is Selmer-only on an open curve over imaginary quadratic fields and the second is about twisted forms and covers. On AI, a reader who treats GPT-5.5’s equations in Theorem 9.8 as needed for Theorem 8.28 would count the Li–Lüdtke result as AI-involved; a reader who treats them as computational support, checked by the authors, would not. A reader who takes the toric paper’s Theorem 1.4 at face value would treat the p-adic toric statement as evidence for hyperbolic curves; one who takes the talk abstract would treat it as only supporting evidence.
what_would_settle_it: The full text of arXiv:2608.20615 Sections 8.3 and 9: whether Theorem 8.28 uses Theorem 9.8 and what ‘discover’ means there, and its acknowledgements. The proof of Theorem 1.4 in arXiv:2409.07923v5 Section 8 and the June 2026 talk abstract. The JTNB PDF of Bresciani’s index-1 paper, to check its AI statement and whether its scope matches arXiv v1. The abstracts of Hoshi’s two 2025 talks. The April 2026 Porowski lecture notes, for the status claim and the cited arXiv:2509.15660. The Pop 2025 t-birational PDF. Any 2026 citing paper for the S-Selmer result and for Betts–Kumpitsch–Lüdtke v2.
